messages:
maria: heads-up — customer 'zen' reported a burst of 401s after their per-tenant API key was rotated at ~02:12 UTC. They see a handful of successes then ~15s windows of 401s repeatedly. opened support ticket.
kevin: can you confirm tenant id + edge region and if there's a CDN in front?
maria: tenant z-17, traffic primarily via eu-west (fastly) with an extra CDN layer. rotation performed by vault-operator rekey job at 2026-03-16T02:12:08Z.
julian: quick hypothesis: CDN or edge proxies holding old Authorization header in connection pool (keepalive) or surrogate-key TTL mis-set. can you paste a sanitized failing response?
maria: repro from their log (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"authentication_failed","message":"api key revoked"}
```
kevin: backend clearly returning revoked. intermittent success points to a partial fleet still using old token. fastly purge + edge conn drain should help.
julian: checked vault-operator logs: rekey event for z-17 at 2026-03-16T02:12:08Z with revocation=true and published revocation webhook to kafka but no automatic CDN purge step.
maria: customer restarted their app containers (rotated client pools) and the 401 spike stopped within ~20s. they still asked for RCA.
kevin: action items now: 1) issue CDN purge for tenant header + path, 2) recommend customers rotate client-side connection pools and short-lived tokens, 3) infra: add keepalive-eviction when we detect revocation.
julian: will prototype a change in hera-edge to force-close upstream keepalive connections for a tenant when we process a revocation event. open PR infra#4976. also instrument a metric auth_revocation_propagation_lag (vault->resolved).
maria: did manual fastly surrogate purge (surrogate-key: tenant-z-17) — got 202 accepted and saw propagation ~10s. customer confirmed green after they restarted.
support-bot: automaton: fastly-purge request id fd8a9 queued -> accepted -> propagated.
kevin: follow-up: we should consider making revocation transactional: after vault mark-revoke, trigger CDN purge and then publish the event. avoids race where clients hit CDN with cached header before purge.
julian: agree — will add atomic purge webhook in the vault-operator path and add unit/e2e tests. ETA: EOD next business day for prototype.
maria: I'll write the customer postmortem summary: root cause = race between vault revocation publication and CDN/edge connection reuse + long-lived upstream keepalives. mitigations = CDN purge webhook, keepalive eviction on revoke, client guidance to use short token TTLs and pool rotation.
kevin: assign julian for infra changes, maria for customer comms. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
